_about: Component spec for pos-pagination (docs/inspect refactor, component migration batch, 2026-08-26). Single source of truth for the Variants/Usage/Tokens tabs on /style-guide "Pagination" section. Reuses the already-curated usage prose from COMP_CONFIGS['pagination'].usage and token data from the existing inspect-pagination.liquid (verified-accurate, currently-live data) restructured into the new schema. Single representative variant — this component's preview shows one instance (no Variant/Base toggle needed per the 2026-08-25/26 "multiple sub-variants side by side" rule). Regenerate the spec partial with the script in RULES.md 6.4 if the source data changes; do not hand-edit token values here. Updated 2026-08-26: hover/focus states added explicitly (duplicating normal) rather than left absent — verified against pos-pagination.css that neither state actually changes any token for non-active page links (no dedicated :hover/:focus-visible color rule exists there at all; the only :hover rule targets the already-active link and keeps its color unchanged). This is a genuine pre-existing accessibility gap (no visible focus indicator on pagination links), tracked separately — not something this spec should paper over by inventing tokens that do not exist in the CSS. Updated 2026-08-27: added usageExample/props/composedOf (Target architecture point 1 fields that were left empty when this spec was first generated).
name: Pagination
description: Splitting long lists, search results, or data tables into discrete numbered pages.
whenToUse: Splitting long lists, search results, or data tables into discrete numbered pages.
The total number of pages is known and users benefit from seeing their position.
whenNotToUse: Fewer than 2 pages of results — do not show pagination at all.
Infinite scroll or "load more" patterns are more appropriate for the content type.
do: Set aria-current="true" on the current page link.
Include a visually-hidden pos-label on the prev/next arrow links so screen readers announce the action.
Wrap the whole component in <nav role="navigation" aria-label="Pagination Navigation">.
dont: Hide the prev/next arrows — they are important for keyboard and screen reader navigation.
Show pagination when there is only one page of results.
accessibility: Every page link must have an aria-label: "Go to page N" for non-current pages, "Current Page, Page N" for the active one.
Prev/next links must have a descriptive accessible name even when they display only an icon.
Surround with <nav> so assistive technology exposes it as a navigation landmark.

props.name: aria-current
props.description: Set on the current page's <a> — also drives its active visual style.

props.name: prev/next visibility
props.description: Hide the previous arrow on page 1 and the next arrow on the last page by omitting the element, not by disabling it.
